name: Benaiah (son of Jehoiada)
title: Solomon's commander and David's loyal warrior
summary: Benaiah was the son of the priest Jehoiada and one of David's most prominent warriors. He was known for his heroic deeds and was later appointed commander-in-chief over Solomon's army, after playing a key role in securing Solomon's accession to the throne.

keyEvents.title: Killed two of Moab's best warriors
keyEvents.description: Benaiah struck down two of Moab's most powerful warriors, establishing his reputation as a fearless fighter.

keyEvents.title: Killed a lion in a cistern
keyEvents.description: On a snowy day, Benaiah went down into a cistern and killed a lion, one of his most legendary feats.

keyEvents.title: Defeated the Egyptian giant
keyEvents.description: Benaiah killed an impressive Egyptian warrior by snatching the spear from his hand and killing him with his own weapon.

keyEvents.title: Leader of David's bodyguard
keyEvents.description: David placed Benaiah over his bodyguard, the Kerethites and Pelethites, showing the great trust the king had in him.

keyEvents.title: Anointed Solomon as king
keyEvents.description: Benaiah was present when Solomon was anointed king at the Gihon spring and supported him against Adonijah's attempt to seize the throne.

keyEvents.title: Executed Solomon's enemies
keyEvents.description: At Solomon's command, Benaiah executed Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei to secure the kingdom and was then appointed commander of the army in Joab's place.
